request.spec:
A user can watch a person (a toggle on the row, per user; PERSON_WATCHED name=<name>,
PERSON_UNWATCHED name=<name>); show watched yes/no for the signed-in user. When a watched
person's claim is settled, approved or re-settled, one line NOTIFY user=<watcher> person=<name>
number=<number> is written per watching user, in the order they started watching, after the
claim's own line and before the rollup lines.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A user can watch a person (a toggle on the row, per user; PERSON_WATCHED name=<name>,
PERSON_UNWATCHED name=<name>); show watched yes/no for the signed-in user. When a watched
person's claim is settled, approved or re-settled, one line NOTIFY user=<watcher> person=<name>
number=<number> is written per watching user, in the order they started watching, after the
claim's own line and before the rollup lines.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Watching is in place, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec (the main "watch and notify" test plus scenarios 1–3).

**What a user sees:** each person's row has a "Watched" cell showing yes/no for the signed-in user, with a Watch/Unwatch button that toggles it. If the change is refused, the row shows its `person-error` element.

**Stored data:** a new migration, `V38__person_watch.sql`, adds a `person_watch` table with one row per (person, user). Stopping watching deletes the row. Watching again adds a new row at the end, so the "order they started watching" is just the row order.

**Server** (new package `net.officefloor.hq.app.watch`):
- **Toggle:** `PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/watch` with body `{on: true|false}` writes `PERSON_WATCHED` or `PERSON_UNWATCHED` with `name=<name>`. It writes nothing if the request changes nothing, for example watching someone already watched.
- **Watched list:** `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/watched?user=<name>` returns the ids of the people that user watches. I made this a separate endpoint rather than a field on the people list, because loading the people list doesn't send who is signed in.
- **Notify lines:** a new step, `NotifyWatchers`, runs in the settle/approve pipeline and in the re-settle pipeline, straight after the claim's own audit line and before the rollup lines. It writes one `NOTIFY user=<watcher> person=<name> number=<number>` per watcher, in watch order. It only fires when the claim actually ends up SETTLED, so a clerk's settle that goes PENDING sends nothing. Bulk settle calls the same settle endpoint for each claim, so it notifies too.

**Front end:** the new cell is in `features/people/watch.slot.tsx`.

**Decision for you:** I kept the usual viewer check on the toggle, so a viewer can't watch anyone. The request didn't say either way, and the tests don't cover it. Watching is a personal preference rather than a change to the sheet, so you might prefer to let viewers watch. That means removing the `guard` step from `watch.PUT.yml`.
